issues.failure_explanation: The limit G(infty)=(C+D)/(C-D/2) is obtained by comparing the leading z^2 coefficients of numerator and denominator, which requires C-D/2 != 0. At the single point C=D=0, which satisfies C+D=0, both leading coefficients vanish; direct evaluation of the amplification factor gives G(z)=(1+z(1/6+(2/3)R(z)))/(1-z/6) -> (5/6)/(-1/6) = -5 as z->infty. Hence G(infty)=-5 (with |G(infty)|=5>1) at C+D=0, falsifying the 'if' direction of the stated equivalence.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the nondegeneracy hypothesis: for (C,D) != (0,0) (equivalently C != 0 on the curve C+D=0), G(infty)=0 iff C+D=0; and note the exceptional value G(infty)=-5 at C=D=0.
issues.overall_effect: The if-and-only-if characterization of the L-stability condition is wrong at (C,D)=(0,0). Downstream uses are unaffected because the imposed curve D=-C is only used with C in [0.018824,0.045589], which excludes 0.
issues.title: Lemma 3.1: equivalence G(infty)=0 iff C+D=0 fails at the point C=D=0
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-clause hypothesis; every application of the lemma in the paper is at C>0, so the scheme, the parameter interval, and all conclusions survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
i.e., all roots of the equation \eqref{equation_C}  lie in the right half-plane,
in another words, the amplification factor $G(z)$ is analytic in $\textnormal{Re}(z)\leq 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The formula Re(z)=(1/3+13C)/(6C) is the real part of the roots of 1-(1/6+13C/2)z+(3C/2)z^2=0 only when the roots are complex conjugates, i.e. when the discriminant (1/3+13C)^2-24C is negative, which happens only for C in (0.00794, 0.08279). For every C<0 the discriminant is positive, the roots are real, and their product 2/(3C) is negative, so one root is strictly negative; e.g. C=-0.1 gives roots approximately -1.43 and 4.65. Thus for all C<-1/39 the denominator of G has a left-half-plane root and G is not analytic in Re(z)<=0, contradicting the lemma. The correct necessary and sufficient condition is C>=0 (positive sum and product of roots).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the condition by C>=0, treating the real-root case via the signs of the sum (1/3+13C)/(3C) and product 2/(3C) of the roots, and delete the branch C<-1/39.
issues.overall_effect: A stated iff criterion for Condition 1 (analyticity of G in the closed left half-plane) is false on its negative branch; a reader choosing C<-1/39 would obtain a method with poles in the stability region. The paper's final interval uses only C>0, where the conclusion holds, so the advertised scheme and Conclusion 3.3 are not invalidated.
issues.title: Lemma 3.2: spurious branch C<-1/39 in the condition for all poles to lie in the right half-plane
issues.why_classification: The fix is a short, local, routine root-sign argument; the lemma's content on the regime actually used (C>=0) is correct, and no dependent result changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Analytically proving $\lvert G(iy)\lvert\leq 1$ for all $y\in\mathbb{R}$ is complex. Instead, we employ a systematic numerical scanning algorithm to determine the A-stability conditions of the scheme.

The parameter space $C \in [0.00, 0.10]$ is discretized into 5,000 sampling points, while the frequency domain along the imaginary axis $y\in [10^{-8}, 10^{4}]$ is densely sampled using 25,000 logarithmically spaced points.

issues.failure_explanation: The Conclusion (a theorem-like block that carries no \label in the source) asserts A-stability, i.e. sup_{Re(z)<=0}|G(z)|<=1, for the whole continuum interval C in [0.018824,0.045589]. Conditions 1 and 3 are argued analytically, but Condition 2, sup_{y in R}|G(iy)|<=1, is checked only by evaluating |G(iy)| at 25,000 logarithmic points over the truncated range y in [10^{-8},10^4] for 5,000 sampled values of C. No continuity or Lipschitz bound, no tail estimate, and no algebraic argument (e.g. nonnegativity of 1-|G(iy)|^2 as a rational function of y^2) bridges the discrete samples to the continuum supremum, so a spike between samples is not excluded and the six-digit endpoints inherit grid-level uncertainty. What is established is only numerical evidence on the sampled set, materially weaker than the stated conclusion.

failure_location.quote: The Implicit TSFO scheme, given by equations \eqref{stage_1}-\eqref{Stage_2}, achieves A-stability under the condition

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either certify Condition 2 rigorously over the interval (e.g. reduce |G(iy)|<=1 to polynomial inequalities in y^2 depending on C and prove their nonnegativity, possibly with interval arithmetic), or restate the Conclusion and the matching prose as numerically verified A-stability on the scanned grid.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central stability guarantee - the A-stability interval for the final scheme (stage_1_final)-(Stage_2_final) and the prose claim 'we derive the final form of this scheme, which is A-stable' - rests on heuristic grid evidence rather than proof.
issues.title: Conclusion 3.3: A-stability interval asserted as established, but Condition 2 is verified only on a finite grid
issues.why_classification: No short routine repair exists: a rigorous fix requires a new, contained but nontrivial analytic argument, and the only source-supported alternative weakens an advertised guarantee (from established A-stability to numerically indicated A-stability). The scheme itself, its fourth order, and a numerically supported stability statement all survive, so it is not serious.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The algorithm identifies the maximum amplification factor across all frequencies and verifies its compliance with the stability criterion $\lvert G(iy)\lvert \leq1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The Conclusion singles out C=0.018924 as 'the optimal parameter' providing 'superior numerical damping characteristics', and this is repeated after the final scheme, but no optimality criterion is defined anywhere in the paper. Under the imposed condition D=-C, every admissible C has identical stiff damping G(infty)=0; and the only metric the scan computes, max_y|G(iy)|, equals 1 for every admissible C because |G(iy)|->|G(0)|=1 as y->0. Hence no quantity in the paper distinguishes C=0.018924; any distinction produced by the scan would be an artifact of the lower frequency cutoff y=10^{-8}. The claim is unsupported by the source.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define an explicit objective (e.g. minimize an error constant, or minimize max_{y>=y0}|G(iy)| over a stated range) and verify the optimum accordingly, or withdraw the optimality claim and present C=0.018924 as one admissible value in the interval.
issues.overall_effect: The recommended parameter value for the final scheme (Stage_2_final) has no justified basis; readers are given an 'optimal' constant with no stated or verified objective.
issues.title: Unsupported claim that C=0.018924 is 'optimal' with 'superior numerical damping'
issues.why_classification: Deleting or qualifying one sentence (in two places) preserves the scheme, the A-stability interval, and every other result; no formal result depends on the claim.

These are different quantities (for the linear test both u_e and u_c are available and differ), so the error metric reported in all convergence tables is ambiguous as written; which definition applies to which table must be inferred from context.

issues.failure_explanation: The eight-dimensional ozone system requires eight initial values, but the specification lists 'u_7(0),' with no assigned value; it is ambiguous whether u_7(0)=0 or u_7(0)=0.0057 is intended (the correction is not forced by the source). diagnostic_evidence.quote: demonstrate that the proposed scheme possesses superior stability regions and smaller numerical errors.
focusing on stable time step size and convergence error

issues.failure_explanation: The text claims that, relative to the classical Implicit RK4 method, the scheme (i) 'reduces the numerical error by about an order of magnitude under identical time steps' and (ii) has 'superior stability regions' that 'enable even larger step sizes', the latter repeated in the Conclusions. Claim (i) is contradicted by the paper's own tables at identical time steps: Robertson at tau/8 has TSFO error 2.33e-12 versus RK4 4.22e-13 (TSFO about 5x worse); ozone at t_end=321.8122 and tau has 5.84e-07 versus 3.77e-08 (about 15x worse); van der Pol at tau has 4.24e-03 versus 3.22e-03 (worse). Claim (ii) is unsupported: the announced comparison 'focusing on stable time step size' never appears in the paper, no stability regions or maximal usable steps are compared, and both methods are A-stable implicit schemes, so no evidence in the source shows larger stability regions or larger stable steps.

failure_location.quote: our scheme reduces the numerical error by about an order of magnitude under identical time steps and offers superior stability that enables even larger step sizes.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the prose to what is shown (fourth-order accuracy with large steps; smaller errors than Implicit RK4 in most tested cases), and either remove the stability-superiority and larger-step claims or substantiate them with stability-domain plots or maximal-step experiments.
issues.overall_effect: The comparative-evaluation narrative (final paragraph of Section 5 and the Conclusions) claims more than the numerical evidence establishes; the demonstrated content is fourth-order accuracy at large steps with smaller errors than Implicit RK4 in most, but not all, tested regimes.
issues.title: Prose overclaims: uniform order-of-magnitude error reduction and superior stability versus Implicit RK4
issues.why_classification: The repair is rewording of two prose passages; no formal result, the scheme, or the tables are affected, and the weakened claims remain recognizably the same.
